newsitem.title: MEXICO: ATHLETICS-MEXICO TO BID FOR 2003 PANAMERICAN GAMES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-MEXICO TO BID FOR 2003 PANAMERICAN GAMES.

text.p: Mexico will seek to host the 2003 PanAmerican Games in the western city of Guadalajara, Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said Wednesday.

"The government will firmly, frankly and permanently support the candidacy of the capital of (the state of) Jalisco as the site of the XV PanAmerican Games in the year 2003," Zedillo said in a speech from the city of Tequila near Guadalajara, Mexico's second-largest city.
The mayor of Guadalajara, Cesar Coll, told reporters earlier Wednesday that his city has the infrastructure and organisational experience to handle such an event.
The PanAmerican Games, held every four years, are staged the year before the Olympics and feature countries from throughout the Americas.
In the past, major sporting events in Mexico, such as the 1968 Olympics and the 1986 World Cup, have been held in Mexico City.
